brief: On October 21, Wiz disclosed PHP2Shell, unauthenticated remote-code-execution flaws (CVSS up to 9.2) present in every PHP version from the last decade, affecting roughly 70% of websites, while Oracle issued an emergency alert for a Java certificate-validation flaw (CVSS 9.1) and LiteLLM suffered its second PyPI/Docker supply-chain attack this year. Goldman's Rich Privorotsky called the pace "somewhat alarming" and wondered if it contributed to that day's AI stock concerns. Separately, Epoch AI data show high-severity CVEs across 21 tech firms running about ten times the 2022-2025 norm since Anthropic's Claude Mythos Preview announcement, and Wiz says frontier models let one researcher match in a week what previously took a team months. Privorotsky concludes this is now bullish for cybersecurity spending, since AI lowers the cost of exploiting flaws while the attack surface grows, reversing March's fear that AI would make defenders obsolete. Separately, Schwab and JPMorgan are restricting unauthorized AI agents on customer accounts; Sacks calls it credential-sharing not attack, Morgan Stanley denies seeing any, and Goldman's Johnstone says liability risk remains regardless. Goldman's FX desk lists both as AI-selloff catalysts, though the piece says the bigger driver is cost of capital, not cyber.
